headline: Sawtooth Wilderness Permits and Lake Access
reservation: Self-issue wilderness permits are generally required at trailheads for day use, but overnight backpacking permits have specific quotas. Developed campgrounds near Redfish Lake frequently sell out six months in advance via official federal booking sites; check the Sawtooth National Forest site for current fire restrictions and area closures.

days.title: Alpine Lakes and Jagged Peaks

stops.name: Redfish Lake
stops.detail: Take the boat shuttle to the far inlet to access the trailhead for high-alpine hikes.

stops.name: Fishhook Creek Trail
stops.detail: A gentler hike through meadows offering views of the iconic Sawtooth spires.

days.driving: Allow 15–30 minutes to trailheads; parking fills very early.
days.note: Boat shuttle operations are seasonal; check current schedules at the lodge.

days.title: River Canyons and High Passes

stops.name: Sawtooth Lake
stops.detail: Climb the steep trail to one of the largest and most scenic lakes in the range.

stops.name: Salmon River
stops.detail: Explore the banks of the 'River of No Return' for fly-fishing or scenic overlooks.

days.driving: Allow 30–50 minutes for mountain road travel; conditions vary.
days.note: Snow can block high-elevation trails well into July; check ranger reports.

days.title: Ghost Towns and Valley Vistas

stops.name: Galena Summit Overlook
stops.detail: Stop for a panoramic view of the headwaters of the Salmon River and the Sawtooth Valley.

stops.name: Custer Ghost Town
stops.detail: Visit this historic mining site within the Land of the Yankee Fork State Park.

days.driving: Allow 60–90 minutes for the traverse between Stanley and Ketchum.
days.note: Mountain passes may be subject to temporary closures for maintenance or weather.

intel.title: Redfish Lake Saturation
intel.text: Main trailhead lots at Redfish Lake often fill by 8 AM in mid-summer. Use overflow areas and be prepared for extra walking to reach the water.

intel.title: Wilderness Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect zero cellular reception once leaving the Highway 75 corridor. Carrying a satellite communication device is suggested for remote wilderness travel.

intel.title: Stanley Supply Gap
intel.text: Stanley has limited fuel stations that may have shorter seasonal hours. Ensure your tank is full before driving over Galena Summit toward Ketchum.

intel.title: Seasonal Thaw
intel.text: High-country lakes often remain frozen until late June. Plan your visit for late July or August to ensure most trails are clear of deep snowpacks.

intel.title: Road Restrictions
intel.text: Highway 21 and 75 are winding mountain routes subject to rockfall and seasonal weather impacts. Check the Idaho Transportation Department for real-time road status.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at SUN and drive 90 minutes north to Stanley. Grocery options are much broader in Ketchum; stock up on major supplies there.
plan.vehicle: An SUV with high clearance is recommended for reaching remote trailheads; check rental terms for driving on unpaved Forest Service roads.
plan.goldenHour: Galena Summit provides an elevated viewpoint for the valley floor, though autumn provides the clearest air for photography.
